newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ING says Barings hits ROE target in Q1.
newsitem.headline: ING says Barings hits ROE target in Q1.

text.p: ING Group NV's British merchant banking unit Barings achieved its targeted return on equity (ROE) in the first three months of 1997, ING executive board chairman Aad Jacobs said on Thursday.
"Over the first three months (of 1997) Barings has made 11 percent ROE, which is in line with our target," Jacobs told a results news conference.
ING Group earlier reported 1996 net profit surged 25.4 percent to a record 3.32 billion guilders.
But Jacobs said Barings had not quite lived up to expectations in 1996.
He said the British merchant bank, which ING bought in March 1995, made a gross contribution to ING 1996 group profits of 120 million guilders.
Of this, 70 million guilders came from ING Barings, with the balance coming from Barings Asset Management.
Barings, which was rescued from near-collapse resulting from unauthorised derivatives trading losses, has been folded into the ING Barings investment banking operation.
"With that (1996 result) Barings has not quite satisfied what we envisaged for it," Jacobs said.
He said the British merchant bank should have recouped its opportunity costs, or what ING could have otherwise earned with its investment of 1.7 billion guilders.
ING would have earned slightly more than 120 million guilders with the money in 1996, Jacobs said.
But he added it had been "quite an achievement" to bring a bank which had been bankrupt up to this level of profitability within three years.
Jacobs also said ING would focus on how best to integrate ING Barings with its corporate banking unit ING Bank International. This was one of the challenges for 1997, he said.
"I think we can make major cost savings there," he told reporters.
